sovereign_country.strategic_role: 北美成熟市场、联邦与省两级公司实体设立（EPC合规）

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Social Commerce via Short Video Platforms

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (Quebec civil law for private law; federal common law for public and criminal law)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP)
Canada–European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA)
Canada–China Agreement for the Promotion and Reciprocal Protection of Investments (FIPA)
Convention between Canada and the United States of America with Respect to Taxes on Income and on Capital (1980, as amended)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, S.C. 2000, c. 17, as amended; Criminal Code, R.S.C., 1985, c. C-46, ss. 462.3 et seq.; Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR, c. P-44.1; Regulation respecting the register of enterprises, CQLR, c. P-44.1, r. 3; Civil Code of Québec, CQLR, c. CCQ-1991, arts. 2182 and 2236–2247 (société en commandite); Special Economic Measures Act, S.C. 1992, c. 17; United Nations Act, R.S.C., 1985, c. U-2; applicable FINTRAC reporting guidance and Canada's sanctions regulations.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing or official attestation from the corporate registry of any foreign corporate general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry or registry authority of the foreign jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille, or consular legalization where the issuing jurisdiction is not a Hague Abolishing the Requirement of Legalisation Convention member

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of the incorporating instrument, certificate of incorporation, and current directors/authorized officers list of each corporate partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign corporate registry, ministry of corporate affairs, or equivalent competent authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille, or consular legalization for non-Hague Convention jurisdictions

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized identity documents, passport pages, and proof of residential address for each individual limited partner and ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or commissioner of oaths in the individual's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille, or consular legalization for non-Hague Convention jurisdictions

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Original power of attorney or mandate appointing a Quebec resident representative and agent for service of process
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notarial authority in the appointing person's jurisdiction, or Quebec notary where mandate is executed in Quebec
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille, or consular legalization and Quebec notarial endorsement where applicable

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Source of funds declaration, bank reference letter, and financial verification for initial contributions and anticipated TikTok Shop payout flows
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Qualified bank, credit union, or regulated financial institution in the source jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized bank officer certification plus Hague Apostille or consular legalization

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-filing screening of every general partner, limited partner, authorized representative, attorney-in-fact, and ultimate beneficial owner against (i) FINTRAC and PCMLTFA domestic politically exposed person categories; (ii) Canadian sanctions lists issued under the Special Economic Measures Act, United Nations Act, and Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act; (iii) OFAC Specially Designated Nationals list; (iv) United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions lists; and (v) additional credible international AML/CFT blacklists. Enhanced due diligence is required for source funds derived from cryptocurrency, high-risk FATF jurisdictions, or outside-regulated banking channels. Screening results, evidence of identity, and findings must be retained for five years and refreshed immediately upon any change of ownership or control.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises / Registre des entreprises du Québec — official online portal: https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca/en
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Charter of the French Language, CQLR, c. C-11, the registered legal name of a Quebec enterprise must be in French or have a preponderant French version. Names in foreign scripts must be transliterated into Latin characters for registration. Non-French descriptive terms are permitted only when no French equivalent exists or when the name is a protected trademark or proper noun. Public-facing signage in Quebec must give clear preponderance to French.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Chambre de commerce / Chamber of Commerce
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The original name reservation may be renewed once for an additional 90 days if the renewal request is filed before expiry. If the Registraire des entreprises rejects a proposed name, the applicant may (i) request written reasons; (ii) file an administrative reconsideration or review application within 30 days, attaching alternative name options, third-party consents, and any required professional-order or ministerial authorization; and (iii) if the refusal is maintained, apply to the Court of Québec for judicial review within 30 days of the final administrative decision. Applicants should submit at least three alternative names with the initial filing to avoid operational delay.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible only when provided by a licensed Quebec corporate services provider maintaining a physical street address in Quebec, a named person available for service of process, and storage for the partnership's statutory records. A pure virtual mailbox or P.O. box without a physical human-accessible office does not satisfy Quebec legal publicity requirements. Online-only TikTok Shop retail does not require a storefront, but a registered office and a Quebec establishment are required.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name search and availability report through Registraire des entreprises
Name reservation for Quebec enterprise (90-day validity)
Notarial drafting of declaration of limited partnership (société en commandite) in French and supporting legal review
Filing fees for legal publicity and issuance of attestation of registration
Registered office and process-agent service for first 12 months
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed corporate services provider / registered agent

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified French translation of foreign company documents and UBO identity papers
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Member of the Ordre des traducteurs, terminologues et interprètes agréés du Québec

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Civil Code of Québec (CQLR c. CCQ-1991), arts. 2236–2255 (société en commandite / limited partnership); Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (CQLR c. P-44.1), ss. 2, 21–24 (mandatory registration of enterprises); Charter of the French Language (CQLR c. C-11), ss. 25–29 (French-language name and public documents).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) – Direction de l'immatriculation
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration d'immatriculation (Declaration of Registration) filed electronically through the REQ 'Mon compte d'entreprise' portal
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital and no escrow account requirement. Contributions are fixed contractually in the limited partnership agreement; each limited partner must contribute cash or property (services are prohibited for limited partners under CCQ art. 2240), and general partners may contribute any lawful value.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the sole general partner of [•] Limited Partnership (the 'Firm'): (i) acknowledges the capital contributions of the initial limited partners as set out in the partnership agreement and records such subscriptions in the partnership register; (ii) adopts as the Firm's registered office the address shown in the declaration of registration filed with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec, being the situs for service of process; (iii) appoints [Name] as principal manager and authorized signatory, and [Name] as alternate signatory, with full authority to open bank accounts and to execute payment-provider agreements, including TikTok Shop Payout and Wise B2B; and (iv) ratifies all pre-formation actions taken in the Firm's name. This resolution takes effect immediately upon adoption.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) – corporate name reservation service (online via an accredited NUANS provider or REQ portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the proposed French-language or bilingual firm name to the REQ NUANS pre-search to confirm uniqueness against existing Quebec business names and trademarks. If the chosen name is available, obtain a 90-day name reservation record and confirm compliance with the Charter of the French Language requirements.
required_dossiers: Identification of the applicant general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is refused for conflict or non-compliance, submit a revised declaration with up to three alternative names accompanied by a new NUANS report; a formal review may be requested from REQ within 30 days after refusal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of the Limited Partnership Agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Not filed with a governmental registry; prepared by civil-law notaries or attorneys admitted in Québec
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the contrat de société en commandite in French (or a bilingual original) containing: the firm name, registered office, declared objects (retail sales via social-media platforms, TikTok Shop), capital contribution schedule, profit-sharing ratios, scope of the general partner's management authority, restrictions on limited partners, and dissolution provisions. Execute the agreement before witnesses; notarization is recommended to facilitate banking and later real-property filings.
required_dossiers: Identification and residential address of each general partner
Identification of limited partners and contribution schedule
Proposed registered office address in Québec
Description of the e-commerce/social-commerce activity (NAICS 454110 / ISIC 4791)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a partner contests the validity of a contribution or clause, cure by executing a rectification amendment (avenant) to the partnership agreement, or, if fundamental error exists, re-execute the agreement with notarial certification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of the Declaration of Registration with the REQ
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) – online filing through 'Mon compte d'entreprise' or in person at 2050, rue de Bleury, Montréal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and submit the Déclaration d'immatriculation for a société en commandite identifying: the general partner's legal name and domicile, the firm's business name, the registered office in Québec, the principal establishment address (which may be the authorized virtual-office location), and the primary business activity code (NAICS 454110). Pay the applicable CAD filing fee online; the declaration takes effect on the date of registration by REQ.
required_dossiers: Name reservation confirmation (if corporate name used)
Proof of Québec registered office (lease, letter of authorization, or ownership deed)
Identification of the responsible natural person signing the declaration
Authorization of attorney-in-fact if filed by a representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If REQ issues a notice of non-compliance or a query, respond within the stated deadline by submitting a corrected declaration (déclaration modificative) with supporting evidence; if the enterprise is struck from the register, apply for reinstatement within 3 years or re-file a new declaration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Receipt of the Attestation of Registration and Québec Enterprise Number (NEQ)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, download the Attestation d'immatriculation and obtain the 10-digit Québec Enterprise Number (NEQ). Verify that all registered particulars (firm name, address, CBCA/CCQ statute code, partners' status) match the executed partnership agreement. Use the attestation for banking, contractual, and tax-identification purposes.
required_dossiers: Copy of executed partnership agreement for internal record
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If data errors are detected on the attestation, file a voluntary dédaration modificative with REQ within 30 days; clerical errors may be corrected without penalty by attaching an explanatory cover letter.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Governance Meeting, Appointment of Officers, and Banking Setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Private act (no government approval); regulated by the partnership agreement and applicable banking anti-money-laundering rules
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first meeting of the general partner; adopt the Pro-Forma First Board Resolution confirming capital subscriptions, registered office, and appointment of authorized signatories. Use the resolution to open a business bank account in the firm's name and to configure payment rails (TikTok Shop Payout, Wise B2B) by completing the platforms' KYB (Know Your Business) verification.
required_dossiers: Notarized/certified copy of the partnership agreement
Valid government-issued photo ID of signatories
Beneficial ownership and ultimate beneficial owner declaration for AML/KYB
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank or payment platform rejects the application for insufficient documentation, submit a supplementary CDD pack (full UBO chain, operating agreements, pro forma invoices) or select an alternate licensed payment processor listed in the firm's approved providers.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Transition to Tax Registration (GST/HST and QST)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Revenu Québec and Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) – Quebec Business Number and tax accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the limited partnership for GST/HST with the CRA and for QST with Revenu Québec within 30 days of registration (or immediately before the first taxable sale). Use the NEQ to obtain the 15-digit Quebec tax identifier; if employees are anticipated, also open payroll source-deduction accounts. This step completes the legal formation cycle and transfers compliance to the tax stage.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late registration triggers penalties under the Excise Tax Act and QST Act; remedy by voluntary disclosure (VDP) to CRA/Revenu Québec before enforcement, paying outstanding amounts and requesting penalty waiver with written justification.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de l'Économie, de l'Innovation et de l'Énergie (MEIE) – Government of Québec; consumer-protection oversight by the Office de la protection du consommateur (OPC)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No statutory operating or manufacturing license is required for a virtual social-commerce retail enterprise under ISIC 4791 (e-commerce resale). Registration with the REQ, GST/HST/QST enrollment, and compliance with the Quebec Consumer Protection Act (CQLR c. P-40.1) distance-selling rules are the sole mandatory clearances. If a physical fulfillment warehouse is later acquired, a municipal occupancy permit is required but no sectoral production license applies.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – a full EIA report is not required for pure e-commerce resale with no manufacturing, effluent discharge, or greenhouse-gas-emitting operations (Environmental Quality Act, CQLR c. Q-2, art. 22). Re-evaluation is triggered only if a fulfillment warehouse with refrigeration or chemical packaging is established, which would then require a MELCCFP attestation of compliance.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable at the formation stage. Should physical warehousing commence, the operator must comply with municipal sewer discharge bylaws, packaging waste diversion standards under the Quebec Residual Materials Management Policy, and VOC emission limits under the Regulation respecting the reduction of VOC emissions (O.C. 1129-2013) where cleaning solvents are used.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Registration with CNESST (Commission des normes, de l'équité, de la santé et de la sécurité du travail) for workplace health and safety is mandatory upon hiring. For a virtual office, only a standard occupancy certificate is required; if warehouse or retail space is leased, municipal fire-safety inspection under the Fire Safety Act (CQLR c. S-3.4), structural load attestation by a licensed Quebec engineer, and accessibility conformity certificates must be obtained before occupation.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) for federal GST/HST via Business Registration Online (available at https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/tax/businesses/topics/register-your-business.html); Revenu Québec administers the Quebec Sales Tax (QST) via its business registration portal at https://www.revenuquebec.ca/en/businesses/.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A limited partnership (or its non-resident representative) must obtain a Canadian Business Number (BN) from the CRA, with a GST/HST program account, using online registration or Form RC1. Mandatory registration is required once annual worldwide taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000; voluntary registration is permitted below this threshold if the partnership otherwise makes taxable supplies in Canada. The partnership must also register separately with Revenu Québec for a QST account using Form SEP-1 (or online via ClicSÉQUR), supplying the partnership agreement, proof of legal existence, and, where necessary, a Canadian agent authorized for service. Non-resident partners of the Canadian limited partnership may additionally require an individual non-resident tax account number and compliance profile with the CRA for reporting Canadian-source income.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not operate a check-the-box or elective entity-classification system under the Income Tax Act. The limited partnership is inherently tax-transparent: it files an information return but computes and pays tax at the partner level. Available statutory elections include subsection 216(1) of the Income Tax Act for non-resident partners to file a Canadian income tax return on a net-basis; elections relating to hybrid mismatch arrangements may require disclosure via Form RC4646 or equivalent; and certain provincial family-farm or fishing partnership elections may be relevant. No general corporate-style check-the-box election is available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (federal Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax) and QST (Quebec Sales Tax) administered by Revenu Québec
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 in annual worldwide taxable supplies (including remote and e-commerce sales); a zero threshold applies to certain non-resident registrants carrying on business in Canada
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction control (CTC), or digital stamping regime exists for GST/HST or QST. Registrants must file GST/HST returns electronically via CRA NETFILE (if sales exceed CAD 1.5 million) and QST returns via Revenu Québec's ClicSÉQUR portal. Invoices must contain prescribed information; records may be kept electronically, but no government-authorised e-invoice pre-clearance is required.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Supplies of goods are zero-rated where they are exported by the registrant within 60 days of the supply (or such longer period as permitted) and proof of export is retained. Services may be zero-rated when performed wholly outside Canada or supplied to a non-resident arm's-length person who is not registered for GST/HST. For social-commerce retail sales, the seller must substantiate the physical movement of goods out of Canada, typically through carrier documentation and customs export evidence.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Form B13A or electronic export declaration)
Inward Remittance Certificate or equivalent proof of payment received from outside Canada
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The CRA and Revenu Québec may reassess and claw back the zero-rating where export documentation is deficient, leaving GST/HST at 5% and QST at 9.975% chargeable on the full value. Knowingly submitting false or misleading information triggers a 50% gross-negligence penalty on the understated net tax, arrears interest, and, in criminal cases, fines of up to CAD 50,000 and imprisonment up to five years under section 327 of the Excise Tax Act. Revenu Québec imposes analogous penalties under the Quebec Sales Tax Act.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) and Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI), with the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) for AML/CFT oversight
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar (CAD) is fully convertible under both current and capital account transactions. Canada maintains an open investment regime under the Investment Canada Act, with no general restrictions on profit remittance, dividend distribution, or capital repatriation for non-resident partners in a Quebec limited partnership. However, cross-border transfers of CAD or foreign currency are subject to FINTRAC reporting for transactions at or above CAD 10,000 or equivalent, and a limited partnership that is a reporting entity under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA) must implement a compliance program. Profit remittance is structurally unimpeded, but withholding tax obligations under Part XIII of the Income Tax Act (Canada) may apply to amounts paid or credited to non-residents, subject to treaty relief under the relevant tax treaty or the Canada-Québec intergovernmental coordination. No exchange control approval is required for ordinary current-account payments, export proceeds, or capital movements, provided the transaction does not involve a sanctioned jurisdiction under the United Nations Act or the Special Economic Measures Act.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory timeline or mandatory conversion ratio for export receipts in Canada. The Bank of Canada and the Department of Finance do not impose any surrender requirement on export proceeds, and a Canadian exporter, including a Québec limited partnership engaged in cross-border TikTok Shop retail, may hold export proceeds in CAD or foreign currency in a domestic or foreign bank account without obligation to convert them into CAD. The only applicable obligations are (i) FINTRAC reporting for cross-border transfers of CAD 10,000 or above, (ii) customs reporting for currency or monetary instruments of CAD 10,000 or above under the Cross-Border Currency and Monetary Instruments Reporting Regulations, and (iii) ordinary corporate and tax accounting requirements under the Income Tax Act and the Taxation Act (Québec). Since the entity is a pass-through limited partnership, the attribution of foreign exchange gains or losses to partners is governed by the partnership agreement and applicable provincial and federal tax rules.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / USD CAD Operating Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High feasibility for licensed non-bank payment service providers and fintech EMIs, subject to compliance with Canada's retail payment oversight framework administered by the Bank of Canada under the Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA), which requires registration as a payment service provider. Offshore digital EMIs that are not licensed in Canada can support a Québec LP on a cross-border basis only as auxiliary payment channels, not as full banking substitutes; they may not accept deposits in Canada and must not hold settlement funds without registration. Wise B2B and similar fintech rails are viable for TikTok Shop payouts and supplier disbursements, but the primary treasury account must be held at a Canadian Schedule I bank or a registered foreign bank branch in Canada to satisfy banking and tax substance requirements.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is required in practice for the first onboarding of a Québec limited partnership at most Canadian Schedule I banks. The general partners, or an authorized signatory with power of attorney issued in accordance with the Civil Code of Québec, may be required to attend a verification meeting either in branch or via a secure video call; however, each bank retains discretion. Remote onboarding is possible for fintech payment service providers, but for a traditional tier-1 commercial bank, the standard mandate is an physical interview for at least one general partner or a designated officer, plus notarized corporate documents, proof of address, and source-of-wealth documentation. Foreign partners cannot rely solely on remote authorization; Canadian banks apply enhanced due diligence for offshore beneficial owners and may require a registered and physically resident Canadian agent or a professional introducer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity with non-resident limited partners
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Partnership register or partnership agreement disclosing all general and limited partners with name, jurisdiction, ownership percentage, control rights, and source of funds; certified copies of government-issued passports or other reliable identification; notarized declarations of source of wealth; confirmation that the entity is not an anonymous shell and that all partners are real persons or entities subject to transparency obligations

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border TikTok Shop revenue flows and third-party marketplace pooling
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed TikTok Shop seller agreement, Shopify/merchant IDs, settlement statements from TikTok Seller Center, historical payout records, reconciliation of refunds, chargebacks and fees, and a clear description of the payment flow from TikTok's settlement bank to the LP's operating account

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume low-value retail e-commerce patterns resembling money laundering or unlicensed money services business activity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Business plan and financial projections, transaction monitoring system or accounting software demonstrating transparent invoicing and inventory matching, no-cash policy documented, customer due diligence policy for B2B counterparties, and FINTRAC registration status if the LP engages in any money services business activities (e.g., currency exchange or transfers outside the ordinary retail exemption)

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Political exposure or sanctions nexus due to international retail customer or supplier base
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: PEP and sanctions screening policy, evidence of automated negative-news screening, end-to-end counterparty list with jurisdiction and legal type, OFAC/UN/Canada sanctions registry verification, and corporate compliance attestation signed by the general partner

Registered office address in Québec, commercial lease or utility bills, payroll or contractor records for Canadian employees, local bank statements, tax registrations (Québec enterprise number / GST-QST numbers), and a board or partners' meeting record evidencing management decisions made in Canada

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections from non-resident partners into the Québec LP must be routed through a Canadian Schedule I bank account using SWIFT MT103 or an equivalent wire with explicit purpose code. For a limited partnership, the recommended code is 'Investment in a Canadian partnership / equity contribution' and the beneficiary must be identified as an unincorporated business. The sending partner should use the partnership's registered name, partnership registration number (Québec enterprise registrar), and account number. A source-of-funds statement and a partnership resolution authorizing the contribution must accompany the inward remittance to satisfy the bank's EDD. CAD 10,000 or above triggers FINTRAC reporting. The capital contribution is not subject to federal or provincial capital tax at the time of injection, but the LP must record the contribution as partners' capital and not as partnership income. For exchange control purposes no permit is required.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements for inventory, logistics, and supplier payments should be cleared via SWIFT MT103 for direct wire transfers, documentary collections, or commercial letters of credit (LC) for high-value imports. Given the TikTok Shop social commerce model, routine supplier settlements will typically use MT103 via the bank's online treasury platform or a payment service provider such as Wise B2B with underlying FX conversion. For LCs, the Québec LP should use a standard irrevocable documentary credit with incoterms stated, issued by the Canadian bank and advised through a correspondent bank in the seller's jurisdiction. Disbursements above CAD 10,000 require FINTRAC reporting if routed as international electronic funds transfers. Dual-use concerns are not present; the primary compliance obligations are valuation, recordkeeping, and documentary support for each payment. Payments to sanctioned jurisdictions are prohibited under Canada's sanctions laws.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Forward exchange contracts (deliverable FX forwards) with a Canadian Schedule I bank or registered derivatives dealer, permitted for hedging anticipated TikTok Shop sales and supplier payables
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) may be employed for exotic or restricted currencies, provided Canadian counterparties are authorized and the contract does not evade sanctions
Cross-currency swaps (FX swaps) between CAD and USD or other G10 currencies, subject to bank credit limits and ISDA/CSA documentation
Plain-vanilla call and put options on major currencies, permitted when used for economic hedging of operating cash flows and aligned with the LP's treasury risk policy
Foreign currency term deposits and natural hedging through multi-currency operating accounts (not derivative instruments but permissible treasury liquidity hedging tools)

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual updating declaration, including required ultimate-beneficiary information
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the end of the limited partnership's financial year; report changes within the separate statutory update period when applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing or non-payment may incur additional fees and statutory penalties and place the partnership in default. Continued non-compliance can lead to administrative cancellation of its registration; confirm the applicable cure period and current penalties with the REQ.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Quebec law does not generally impose an independent audit on every limited partnership based on revenue or asset thresholds. An audit may be required by the partnership agreement, financing terms, investor requirements, or another applicable law.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: No universal statutory financial-reporting framework applies to every Quebec limited partnership. Where financial statements are prepared, Canadian ASPE is commonly used for private entities; IFRS may be selected where appropriate. Tax reporting follows applicable Canadian federal and Quebec tax rules.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Review ultimate-beneficiary and partnership information at least annually and report required changes to the REQ within the applicable statutory period. Confirm or update the information through the annual updating declaration; disclose changes in partners or ownership where required.
